subject: science
topic: Humans did not evolve from chimpanzees
angle: The evidence shows that humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor, with various studies providing different estimates for when that split occurred.
title: The Shared Ancestor

hooks.text: Did you evolve from a chimpanzee?
You think we came from them. We share an ancestor.
You are ignoring the common ancestor in your own DNA.
A hand reaching for a leaf in a dark forest.

reveal.headline: Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor.
reveal.body: Evidence from multiple studies shows that humans did not evolve from chimpanzees. Instead, both species branched off from a shared ancestor.

explain.headline: The split happened millions of years ago.
explain.body: Different models provide different dates for this divergence. Some studies date the split to 4.

matters.headline: Your lineage is a shared history.
matters.body: That may be why you see similarities in behavior. You are not a descendant of the modern chimpanzee, but a cousin who shared a beginning.

example.headline: A hand grasping a tool.
example.body: You hold a glass of water. Your ancestors used plants to probe and sponge, long before stone tools appeared in the record.

question.headline: What part of your ancestry do you still carry?

claims.text: Humans diverged from chimpanzees 4.6 my ago and that the human and chimpanzee clade diverged from the gorilla 7.2 my ago.
claims.quote: The ML analysis of two species shows that humans diverged from chimpanzees 4. 6 my ago and that the human and chimpanzee clade diverged from the gorilla 7. 2 my ago.

claims.text: The human-chimpanzee split is dated to at least 7-8 million years.
claims.quote: We date the human-chimpanzee split to at least 7-8 million years and the population split between Neanderthals and modern humans to 400,000-800,000 y ago.

claims.text: The common ancestor of living Pan apes likely used plant tools for probing, sponging, and display, but it did not use stone tools.
claims.quote: This method indicates that the common ancestor of living Pan apes likely used plant tools for probing, sponging, and display, but it did not use stone tools.

claims.text: The most parsimonious model for the evolution of hominin shoulder shape starts with an African ape-like ancestral state.
claims.quote: We show that the most parsimonious model for the evolution of hominin shoulder shape starts with an African ape-like ancestral state.

claims.text: Derivation of habitual terrestrial bipedality from arboreal hand-assisted bipedality requires fewer transitions, and is also kinematically and kinetically more parsimonious.

verdict: The sources provide multiple independent methods and models that consistently point to a common ancestor for humans and chimpanzees, though they differ on the specific timing of the divergence.
caveat: The specific date of the human-chimpanzee split varies significantly between different models, ranging from 4.6 million years to at least 7-8 million years.
